The rise of periphrastic do

Source: R/data.R
do_support.Rd

Use of do (Did he go?, He did not go) in 300 texts dated 1400 to 1700, in four sentence types: the number of clauses with do out of all eligible clauses. In three contexts the change follows S-curves with the same slope and different starting points (the Constant Rate Effect). Affirmative declaratives barely take part.

Usage

do_support

Format

A tibble with 1200 rows and 5 columns:

text

Text ID, T001 to T300.

year

Year of the text.

context

"affirmative declarative", "negative declarative", "affirmative question" or "negative question".

do

Clauses with do.

eligible

All clauses in this context in this text.

Source

data-raw/do_support.R

Details

True model, in log-odds: baseline + 0.035 * (year - 1550) (3.5 per century in every context), with baselines 1.0 (affirmative questions), 1.6 (negative questions), -0.6 (negative declaratives) and -7.5 (affirmative declaratives), and by-text intercepts (SD 0.4). In the historical data, do in affirmative declaratives later declined again; the simulation leaves this out.

References

Ellegård, A. (1953). The auxiliary do: The establishment and regulation of its use in English. Stockholm: Almqvist & Wiksell.

Kroch, A. S. (1989). Reflexes of grammar in patterns of language change. Language Variation and Change, 1(3), 199-244. doi:10.1017/S0954394500000168

Examples

do_support$century <- (do_support$year - 1550) / 100
m <- glm(cbind(do, eligible - do) ~ 0 + context + context:century, data = do_support,
         family = binomial)
round(coef(m), 2)
#>         contextaffirmative declarative            contextnegative declarative 
#>                                  -7.35                                  -0.63 
#>            contextaffirmative question               contextnegative question 
#>                                   1.02                                   1.61 
#> contextaffirmative declarative:century    contextnegative declarative:century 
#>                                   3.46                                   3.50 
#>    contextaffirmative question:century       contextnegative question:century 
#>                                   3.52                                   3.45 
rising <- subset(do_support, context != "affirmative declarative")
anova(glm(cbind(do, eligible - do) ~ context + century, data = rising, family = binomial),
      glm(cbind(do, eligible - do) ~ context * century, data = rising, family = binomial),
      test = "Chisq")
#> Analysis of Deviance Table
#> 
#> Model 1: cbind(do, eligible - do) ~ context + century
#> Model 2: cbind(do, eligible - do) ~ context * century
#>   Resid. Df Resid. Dev Df Deviance Pr(>Chi)
#> 1       896     969.09                     
#> 2       894     968.92  2  0.17152   0.9178
